Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, daily pool data demonstrates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

According to recent reports, daily pool data demonstrates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

Industry observers note that according to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

According to recent reports, the deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

Industry observers note that NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

It has been revealed that the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

Industry observers note that as of ZecStats' latest enhancement on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

It has been revealed that small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who initiative to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

Sources indicate that in practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. People need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

It has been revealed that that has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

Industry observers note that the useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Geekwire ↗ Open Full Page

What went wrong with Outlook: Microsoft blames ‘thundering herds’ and a bug unnoticed for months

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 16, 2026 at 7:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 7:31 am.
  • Microsoft’s own safety systems helped turn a dormant software flaw into last week’s global Outlook outage, rerouting traffic from failing servers onto healthy ones that had the same problem, until more than 80% of the servers in its Microsoft 365 networking gateway had stopped responding.
  • That phenomenon, known as a cascading failure, is one of the findings in Microsoft’s preliminary report on the outage, released overnight, dissecting the failure that cut off email for people and organizations in more than 70 countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 16, 2026 at 7:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 7:31 am.

Microsoft’s own safety systems helped turn a dormant software flaw into last week’s global Outlook outage, rerouting traffic from failing servers onto healthy ones that had the same problem, until more than 80% of the servers in its Microsoft 365 networking gateway had stopped responding.

That phenomenon, known as a cascading failure, is one of the findings in Microsoft’s preliminary report on the outage, released overnight, dissecting the failure that cut off email for people and organizations in more than 70 countries.

According to the report, the attempts to recover were further complicated by a second problem: servers that engineers restarted were immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and stopped responding again, a phenomenon known as a “thundering herd.”.

Microsoft indicates active service disruptions lasted nearly 24 hours. Delayed email continued to be delivered after service returned Friday morning, and the firm posted its public all-clear on X late Friday night, nearly 38 hours after the outage began.

The underlying flaw dates to July, when Microsoft began rolling out a fix to the software that handles incoming connections on its networking gateway, the servers that sit in front of Outlook and many other Microsoft 365 services.

Sources indicate that microsoft hasn’t stated what the fix was meant to address. It ran worldwide for more than three months without problems, according to the report.

Under heavy load, however, parts of that software could get stuck waiting on one another, using up the servers’ processing power and memory until they froze.

That’s what happened last week. About 15 hours before the outage, Microsoft’s systems automatically moved Teams traffic onto the same servers that handle Outlook email, adding to their load, according to the report. Microsoft called the switch part of normal operations but didn’t say what prompted it.

Complicating matters, nearly 14% of the gateway’s server capacity was already out of service because of an unrelated problem, which also isn’t detailed in the report.

According to recent reports, when traffic peaked during the U.S. workday, that was enough to trigger the outage.

Two things stand out as likely areas of scrutiny:.

Microsoft’s testing didn’t catch the bug. Its labs mostly used less powerful machines with fewer processing cores, running a different mix of traffic, while the problem was worst on the newer servers handling real customer load.

The fix also passed through Microsoft’s standard staged rollout, spreading worldwide over several weeks without any sign of trouble, according to the report.

The company certainly has the means to test on the hardware it actually runs. It spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures in its most recent quarter, much of it on AI infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that the safeguards meant to contain the damage didn’t hold. Walls between regions failed because of what the report calls “a separate concern,” which it doesn’t explain, so the outage went global.

The gateway is made up of thousands of “capacity units” grouped into regions, with walls between them meant to keep a failure in one place. Microsoft also runs a second, independent gateway so services can switch over during a disruption.

In a recent development, teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps made that switch, which is why Teams chats and meetings mostly kept working. Exchange couldn’t, “for scale reasons,” as the manufacturer put it, so email stayed down.

Sources indicate that microsoft’s own tools added to the problem. Its automated recovery “was not designed” for a fleet that was almost entirely unresponsive, according to the report, and its usual ways of rolling back a bad change couldn’t quickly undo one that was months old.

The company’s systems automatically shifted traffic from unresponsive servers to healthy ones, and the extra load triggered the same bug on those servers, too. About 10 hours in, engineers turned off some of that automatic rerouting.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, posted an abridged version of the report on X late Sunday. “We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations,” he wrote.

Lamanna had previewed the findings Friday afternoon, blaming “cascading failures + thundering herds at our network perimeter” for the slow recovery, as GeekWire reported when Microsoft declared the outage over.

Microsoft states it has rolled back the defective code, added server capacity and monitoring, and put new limits on how traffic is redistributed to avoid another cascade. A final report with a full list of repairs is due Nov. 20.

Sources indicate that it may also answer the biggest question the preliminary report leaves open: why the walls between regions didn’t stop the outage from spreading worldwide. Microsoft blames that on “a separate glitch,” apart from the July bug, but hasn’t stated what it was.

Industry observers note that while a considerable amount of their exploits has been frozen in place, especially USDT and USDC, on-chain BTC and ETH transfers are virtually impossible to block. It was the largest crypto exploit in history by dollar value and has caused the market to lose more than 20% of its value since.

The use of cross-chain bridges like THORChain has reignited the debate around these automated, decentralized services. Broader industry scrutiny means these services could come under pressure in the near future. Already, US agencies like the FBI have urged the chain’s node operators to block addresses associated with the hack.

However, there is no solution to this loophole in sight. Critics argue that even if the Bitcoin and Ethereum connected to these exploit wallets cannot be touched in a decentralized economy, they should be prevented from using platforms like THORChain to try to mix and legitimize their illegitimate funds. Eventually, the crypto will end up in centralized exchanges, where it can be blocked and returned to the affected Binance exchange.

Industry observers note that furthermore, the popular use of these cross-chain bridges is influencing liquidity in THORChain pools and contributing to a broader market price squeeze. Initially, it was predicted that a large chunk of the stolen crypto would be frozen for some time, but the sudden exodus has put further pressure on the market, affecting smaller digital currencies more than larger ones.

Hopes of recovering the funds are not lost, as trackers continue to pursue them with the help of automation.

Industry observers note that that monthly decline was almost twice the latest $16.5 billion contraction. Back in 2022, the damage continued into the following year. By September 2023, aggregate stablecoin supply had fallen by 26% from its March 2022 peak, a contraction of $43 billion.

Bitcoin endured a similar period of weakness. After reaching nearly $69,000 in November 2021, BTC eventually plunged to around $15,500 in November 2022. Stablecoin supply continued shrinking even after the initial market shock initiated by Terra. Crypto’s liquidity problems then became a prolonged market condition.

According to recent reports, yet, in 2023, not every stablecoin experienced the same fate. USDT supply rose $13.3 billion from its November 2022 lows, while USDC lost $16.7 billion. During that period, investors were not simply abandoning every stablecoin. Some were moving toward Tether as the market reassessed issuers and available returns.

In a recent development, this time, arguably, the stablecoin contraction is happening against a different market backdrop. Crypto traders have fewer reasons to keep large amounts of capital parked in stablecoins when Bitcoin and major altcoins struggle to attract buyers. Some holders may be redeeming their tokens for traditional dollars, while others are moving into interest-bearing assets outside crypto.

A shrinking stablecoin market does not mean every dollar has left digital assets. But the simultaneous decline in USDT and USDC supply makes the latest contraction harder to dismiss as simple rotation between issuers.

A crypto recovery needs buyers willing to commit fresh capital, and stablecoins have historically provided traders with an immediate way to enter the market.

Amazon picks its Bond: Robert Pattinson to play 007, ending years of speculation over coveted role

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 16, 2026 at 8:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 8:32 am.
  • Last year, Jeff Bezos asked social media, “Who’d you pick as the next Bond?” Amazon now has its own answer: Robert Pattinson.
  • The 40-year-old Pattinson — best known for “Twilight,” “The Batman” and this summer’s “The Odyssey” — becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 16, 2026 at 8:31 amNovember 16, 2026 at 8:32 am.

Last year, Jeff Bezos asked social media, “Who’d you pick as the next Bond?” Amazon now has its own answer: Robert Pattinson.

The 40-year-old Pattinson — best known for “Twilight,” “The Batman” and this summer’s “The Odyssey” — becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series. He takes over from Daniel Craig, whose fifth and last Bond film, “No Time to Die,” came out in 2021.

In a recent development, amazon got a 50% stake in the Bond films when it bought MGM for $8.5 billion in 2022, and it took creative control last year in a joint venture with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson. Fans and bookmakers had been guessing about Craig’s successor since he stated in 2019 he was leaving the role.

Over the years, the rumored contenders included Idris Elba, Tom Hardy, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Tom Holland and Henry Cavill. By the end, there were five finalists. Pattinson beat out Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner after screen tests in London in late October, according to The Latest York Times. Casting director Nina Gold ran the tests, which covered stunts, dialogue and camera presence.

Bond is one of the most valuable properties Amazon got in the MGM deal, its second-largest acquisition ever behind Whole Foods. The franchise has earned nearly $7 billion at the domestic box office, adjusted for inflation, since “Dr. No” in 1962. Now Amazon is running it without the Broccoli family, whose stewardship over six decades built it into one of Hollywood’s biggest moneymakers.

Pattinson’s casting is the most visible move yet in Amazon’s looks for Bond. As the Times noted, the 2025 deal followed years of behind-the-scenes friction over Amazon’s ambitions to expand the Bond universe beyond the films. The Times also pointed out that Amazon has to win over a generation of moviegoers who grew up during the franchise’s long hiatus and gravitated toward superheroes, horror movies and video game adaptations.

In a recent development, amazon is already putting the back catalog to work. Alongside Monday’s announcement, it published a guide to streaming the 007 films on Prime Video.

Identity Confirmed pic.twitter.com/FCU5A9c1wk.

In a recent development, to lead the next film, Amazon brought in producers Amy Pascal, the former Sony Pictures chairwoman, and David Heyman, who produced all eight “Harry Potter” movies. Denis Villeneuve (“Dune”) is directing from an original screenplay by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight. No release date has been set, and the Times reports that a theatrical release before 2028 is unlikely.

Industry observers note that “Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond,” Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, mentioned in a statement. Hopkins said Pattinson’s “remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice” to carry on the 007 legacy.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”.

Some longtime fans have worried that under Amazon, Bond will lose his distinctly British character and become more corporate and American, the Times reported. Pascal and Heyman, in a joint statement, called the English actor “the perfect Bond for our times.”.

Bezos had yet to weigh back in on social media about Amazon’s pick, but Amazon CEO Andy Jassy did in a LinkedIn post, writing that he was “excited” to have Pattinson in the role, calling him “one of the most versatile actors of his generation, who consistently makes fearless choices, and keeps surprising people with his performances.”.

Fans online were split. Some posted images of Elba or Cavill, calling Pattinson as 007 a “huge miss.” Others said the actor was on a “generational run” right now with the roles he’s landing. Others shared GIFs of Sean Connery, saying there will only ever be one Bond.

Recent findings suggest that I checked in with my mom, a longtime Bond lover and the biggest movie fan I know. She quickly responded via text.

“No way … not sexy enough for me,” she wrote of Pattinson. “I really liked Daniel Craig, but Sean Connery has always been a favorite.”.

Recent findings suggest that lee shared a Bloomberg and Fundstrat chart that compares the price of ETH ahead of the SpaceX IPO in June with the current decline. SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO in June. The bottom for ETH came three trading days before SpaceX priced its shares, and the price of ETH went up after that.

Industry observers note that anthropic is set to price its IPO on Nov. 18 and aims to raise up to $64.4 billion. It would be the second-largest IPO in history after SpaceX.

Lee blamed the decline of ETH on a rotation of money into the Anthropic IPO, and Binance founder Changpeng Zhao and Strive CEO Matt Cole have pointed to the same flow of liquidity. On Monday, ETH is trading at $1,823.

Recent findings suggest that bitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), which Lee chairs, has bought ETH every week since it released its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025. In its Nov. 16 revision, the company disclosed fresh numbers: it added 7,653 ETH to its reserves last week and 9,587 ETH the week before.

BitMine now holds 6,077,745 ETH, or 4.97% of all coins in circulation (about 122.2 million ETH), and it is the world's largest corporate Ethereum treasury. According to the organization, it is 99% of the way through its "Alchemy of 5%" program, and fewer than 35,000 ETH are left to reach the target.

The total portfolio of BitMine, which includes crypto, cash, securities and venture stakes, has shrunk from a peak of more than $14 billion to $11.8 billion. According to BitMine, 5,227,037 ETH, or around 86% of the reserve, is staked.

Lee expects the growth cycle for ETH to last two to three years, driven by bank tokenization, and his base-case targets for ETH range from $12,000 to $22,000.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.
  • On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still states Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.
  • Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still states Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

It has been revealed that most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It notes: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

Industry observers note that the schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the organization wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide states "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

In a recent development, the main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

According to recent reports, circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

According to recent reports, as of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle remarked "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Industry observers note that many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

It has been revealed that the fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

It has been revealed that for teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

In a recent development, for Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

In a recent development, for everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

Despite posting a solid earnings beat, Elastic sees its stock slide on rough guidance

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.
  • In a recent development, the tech giant reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents.
  • According to recent reports, the results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:33 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.

In a recent development, the tech giant reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents. Revenue rose 17%, to $496 million, surpassing the Street’s target of $487 million.

According to recent reports, the results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability. Its net income for the quarter came to $171 million, rebounding from a loss of $51.3 million in the same period one year ago.

However, investors were less than impressed with the company’s guidance. For the quarter in progress, Elastic mentioned it’s looking for earnings of between 90 cents and 92 cents per share on sales of $507.5 million to $508.5 million. That’s some way below the Street’s targets of 95 cents in earnings and $517.6 million in revenue. The company is not helped by the weak Euro, with currency conversions likely to cause a $4.5 million headwind on revenue in the quarter.

The full-year picture is not much better, as Elastic forecast annual sales of between $2 billion and $2.01 billion compared with the Street’s model of $2.01 billion.

Netherlands-based Elastic is one of Europe’s most successful software companies. It’s the developer of the popular open-source enterprise search platform Elasticsearch, which is used by thousands of businesses all over the world. The base platform is free to download and use, with Elastic making money by selling a special cloud-hosted version that ships with premium features not available in the open edition. The company also sells application observability and security tools.

In the last couple of years, Elastic has tried to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom by positioning Elasticsearch as a useful cog in the wheel that feeds real-time data into large language models to provide them with business context. A key capability is Elastic Context Engine, which gathers, structures, and serves business-specific context to AI agents so they can make accurate decisions with fewer tokens and lower latency.

More recently, the company has built AI-native products including AlertZero, which enables enterprises to orchestrate teams of autonomous security agents that automate tasks around data protection and threat hunting.

Elastic Chief Executive Ash Kulkarni (pictured) said he’s excited about the potential of those new capabilities to drive significant revenue over time. “Elastic delivered another strong quarter, beating guidance across all key metrics,” he said. “Our strong results reflect expanding customer adoption and position us well to continue our strong execution in the back half of fiscal 2027.”.

Unfortunately for Kulkarni, investors didn’t seem to share his enthusiasm. The market was clearly expecting trouble on the horizon in the hours before the tech giant published its report, as its stock declined 8% during regular trading. Once the results were out, it fell another 8% after-hours. That means Elastic’s stock is now up just over 1% in the year to date.

Industry observers note that elastic’s stock had rallied more than 150% between April and October, but virtually all of those gains have now been erased. Prior to today, the shares had already lost more than 20% this month amid broader concerns about the AI industry. Some investors continue to worry about the potential of AI technology to challenge the business models of software companies.

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 16, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 17, 2026 at 3:48 pm.

According to recent reports, A Harvard-led study estimates that electricity use at 403 U.S. hyperscale data centers was equal to roughly 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions — a volume roughly comparable to Denmark’s carbon footprint.

The research examined some of the nation’s largest and most powerful data center facilities operating between May 2024 and April 2025. Together, those facilities accounted for an estimated 1.8% of total U.S. electricity consumption.

“What we’re seeing is already striking, but it’s only a snapshot of a rapidly expanding industry,” Gianluca Guidi, the study’s lead author and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, said in a statement.

Guidi noted that the data center boom has continued since the study period ended. “That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we’re reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026.”.

The research, published in the journal Nature Sustainability and explored in an associated website, comes amid growing pushback and concerns about the facilities’ impacts on electric bills, water consumption, noise and carbon emissions.

In the Pacific Northwest, government officials are enacting moratoriums and exploring legislation to regulate data center development. Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek in October directed a state agency to pause processing and issuing permits for fresh and expanding data centers until July 2027. In Washington, state Rep. Beth Doglio, D-Olympia, will propose data center rules in the legislative session that starts in January.

Hyperscale sites handle massive computing workloads and data storage, supporting operations including large language model training and AI deployment.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers found that Oregon ranked second in electricity used by hyperscale data centers in the study, consuming about half as much as those in Virginia. Given Oregon’s access to clean hydropower, the state ranked sixth in carbon dioxide emissions attributed to the facilities’ electricity use. The publication highlighted data from the top 10 states for energy use, which does not include Washington.

According to recent reports, nationwide, roughly 54% of the electricity attributed to the facilities came from fossil fuels, primarily natural gas and coal. The estimates were based on regional power generation mixes, not individual operators’ clean energy purchases.

In a recent development, the study did not break out energy use by data center operator. Amazon, Microsoft and Google have the largest data center footprints worldwide and account for 57% of hyperscale data center capacity, according to Synergy Research Group.

It has been revealed that all three have aggressive carbon reduction targets. While their emissions have all increased in recent years, the companies say they remain committed to their goals. Microsoft and Amazon point to their support for upcoming clean power projects and investments in low-carbon building materials for the facilities as positive steps towards reductions.

“We continue to really be focused around carbon negativity by 2030,” Melanie Nakagawa, Microsoft’s chief sustainability officer, told GeekWire in July.

Kara Hurst, Amazon’s chief sustainability officer, acknowledged that it will be difficult for the tech giant to reach its target of net-zero emissions by 2040.

Industry observers note that “So that is a real challenge,” Hurst noted in September, “and we’re here to meet the moment. I’m not saying that it’s going to be easy, and I’m not saying it’s going to be linear. But we’re going to put everything we have behind that.”.

In a recent development, at the same time, both tech giants are pursuing projects involving fossil fuel energy in Texas. Microsoft in June signed a 20-year deal to purchase power from a natural gas facility slated to come online in 2028. Amazon has agreed to become the anchor tenant of a massive planned data center campus with proposed natural gas and nuclear power generation, according to the Financial Times.

Recent findings suggest that “Assessing the Carbon Emissions and Energy Consumption of US Hyperscale Data Centers” published in Nature Sustainability and researchers from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, University of Pisa, IMT School of Advanced Studies, Aurora Energy Research, Environmental Systems Research Institute, Baxtel and UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

ScienceOra will continue to refine its product experience around the needs of international users, making access to research tools and scientific exploration more seamless.

Explore ScienceOra: https://www.scienceora.ai.

ScienceOra is Wenge AI's AI-powered scientific research and decision-support platform. Wenge AI (1956.HK) is an enterprise AI firm developing proprietary foundation models and AI platforms to help organizations turn advanced AI capabilities into practical business applications. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Danish parliament unanimously approved a security deal with Trump on Thursday, which would allow the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that trump has repeatedly threatened to take over Greenland since his second term began.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, president Donald Trump is one step closer to his goal of expanding U.S. military presence across Greenland, but it may be costing America its relationship with Europe, long after Trump leaves the White House.

The Danish parliament unanimously approved a security deal with Trump on Thursday, which would allow the U.S. to have at least two additional military bases on Denmark’s autonomous territory of Greenland, as well as the construction of infrastructure for the “Golden Dome,” a multilayer missile defense system. Trump and the Danish and Greenlandic prime ministers initially signed the agreement in September. The pact still needs formal notification from the U.S. before it takes effect.

Recent findings suggest that trump has repeatedly threatened to take over Greenland since his second term began. He has argued that the country’s positioning between Russia and the U.S. creates the need for a strong American military presence to potentially track and intercept missiles. The island also is abundant in rare earths that have become more accessible as climate change melts the polar ice in the area.

Sources indicate that tensions between Trump and Denmark peaked in January, when the president refused to rule out military force in pursuit of the island, alarming not just Danish and Greenlandic authorities, but also longtime allies in NATO, especially because the U.S. and Denmark have had a longstanding defense agreement in place since 1951, which already outlines a path for the U.S. to grow and maintain a military presence on the island. Trump ruled out force days later, in a Jan. 21 speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

Sources indicate that but foreign policy experts warn that while the fresh security deal effectively expands upon the concessions from the 1951 agreement and marks a de-escalation of tensions between the U.S. and Denmark, the prolonged friction surrounding Greenland will have lasting negative consequences on the U.S.

“I don’t think that it has been worth the cost,” Mikkel Runge Olesen, a senior researcher at the Danish Institute for International Studies in Copenhagen, told Fortune. “This crisis has been absolutely devastating for U.S.-Danish relations, for U.S.-Greenlandic relations, and for U.S. European relations in general. I think that the damages that this crisis has caused will endure long after Trump leaves office.”.

The Trump administration has heightened strain between the U.S. and Europe throughout the president’s second term, including pushing European rearmament on the grounds that the U.S. no longer was interested in providing as much military aid and was divesting from efforts to defend Ukraine. The U.S. is also warning that a $3.4 billion European Investment Bank Loan to Airbus  could break a truce in a long-running aircraft subsidy fight and put its broader trade deal with the EU at risk.

In a recent development, when Trump escalated tensions between the U.S. and Greenland in January, the conflict became a broader European issue, Olesen argued. Following Trump’s assertions, the Netherlands, Greece, Luxembourg, Slovenia and other European nations issued joint statements in support of Greenland. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen meanwhile warned that if a U.S. military offense against Greenland were to come to fruition, it would end NATO.

Sources indicate that “There was a moment where it sort of became a rallying cry for opposition to the U.S.” Olesen said. “From a European perspective, all those things sort of pull in the same direction. You can say, ‘Well, the Greenland crisis was one episode out of a few, right?’ But it was probably one of the few big ones.”.

In a recent development, experts have warned the “Golden Dome,” intended to be partly modeled after Israel’s “Iron Dome,” also risks being a greater financial burden than anticipated. An analysis from the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) found the defense system is projected to cost $1.2 trillion to build and operate over 20 years, far exceeding Trump’s initial $175 billion estimate. Steve Fetter, a professor of public policy at the University of Maryland, argued that the technology behind the dome may not even be very effective, as Russia and China could overwhelm the system by barraging it with cheap missiles or find other means of skirting its defenses, making it not just an expensive undertaking, but one that may provide little protection.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced security deal does hold some advantages over the 1951 agreement, Olesen explained. Most importantly, he stated, is that the agreement will protect U.S. resource extraction by restricting foreign investments from non-NATO and non-European Union partners, which creates a greater barrier for adversaries like China to invest in Greenland. While Denmark and Greenland were already shifting away from Chinese investments, the deal effectively safeguards China’s exclusion.

Sources indicate that the agreement also includes written assurances outlining the modernization of the U.S. Pituffik Space Base, as well as latest defense areas in the Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig regions of the island. Per the treaty, Greenland is still a territory of Denmark and if it were to pursue its independence, it must remain under NATO. While Greenland was still likely to be part of the alliance anyway, the agreement removes any uncertainty for the U.S.

Recent findings suggest that trump may also see the treaty as a victory for more symbolic reasons, Garret Martin, co-director of the Transatlantic Policy Center at American University, told Fortune. The U.S. military presence on Greenland does indeed hold military significance, but the assurance of greater defense on the island is likely more key to Trump than the rest of his administration, Martin argued. He likened the security agreement to former President Barack Obama’s 2015 Iran nuclear deal, a since-collapsed pact for Iran to restrict its nuclear program in order to receive economic sanctions relief: After a common midterms defeat, the White House usually shifts to implementing policies where they can have a signature achievement or lasting policy.

“He’s very much a wounded political beast because of the rout in the midterms,” Martin remarked.

“But he still has two years, and foreign policy is still the area where the president has and will keep major influence.”.

Industry observers note that I’m an AI engineer and I’m currently building ChatMakr, an AI-powered platform that creates multi-agent chatbots in seconds. I also built Rune Score, a sports analytics chatbot, and it cost me $0.

In a recent development, from the outside, it looks like a simple chatbot. Under the hood, it’s a distributed system that has to handle the freshness of sports data, user rephrasing, extraction failures, LLM call costs, streaming, memory, fallbacks and security. Here’s the stack I actually used to build it layer by layer, what I did with each tool and what’s free about it.

According to recent reports, before writing a line of code, a chatbot needs a face. I used Figma to generate the chatbot’s logo straight from a text prompt describing the style and mood I wanted, then iterated on it a few times inside Figma itself rather than handing it to a designer. Figma’s own free plan covers individual use with unlimited file storage.

The whole project lives in a GitHub repository, private while the chatbot was still rough, and it’s the same repo both Claude and Codex connect to. GitHub’s free initiative gives unlimited private repositories with a limited feature set and 2,000 minutes a month of Actions included on GitHub Free for standard runners on private repos, enough to run tests and basic automation without hitting a wall. Standard runners on public repositories stay free no matter how much you use them.

Recent findings suggest that claude Code did the actual building, the chatbot’s backend and the AI agents running inside it. I kept it connected directly to the GitHub repository and never let it touch the main branch directly: every task ran on its own branch, and nothing merged until I’d reviewed the diff myself and approved the pull request. The genuine free route in is a Guest Pass: if someone you know already pays for Claude Max, they can send you one, and it unlocks a full week of free Pro-level access.

Sources indicate that I gave Codex a different job, connected to the same repository but never writing production code itself. It reviewed what Claude had actually shipped, acting as an independent judge on pull requests, and I also used it to draft the next development prompt I’d hand back to Claude, effectively having one model strategy the work and another execute it. Codex has a genuine free plan at $0 a month. Free accounts run on GPT-5.6 Terra, OpenAI’s cost-efficient model for that tier. The free plan is capped at a usage limit rather than a time limit, which is exactly the size of job a reviewer role needs.

I bought the chatbot’s domain name through Cloudflare, where registration is usually cheap since Cloudflare sells at cost with no markup, and kept the DNS in the same place rather than splitting it across providers. From there I used Cloudflare’s free security layer to protect the domain, including rate limiting rules to stop any single source from hammering the chatbot’s endpoints. Cloudflare’s WAF documentation covers exactly this kind of rule, and the core protections, DNS, DDoS protection, and basic security features, are included on the free plan.

I used Railway for both the backend and the frontend, with a separate test environment so I could ship changes rapidly without risking the live version. New accounts get a one-time free credit grant before any card is required, and unlike some free hosts, Railway doesn’t put your service to sleep by default the way its own documentation describes for its optional Serverless feature, so there’s no cold start tax on the free tier unless you turn that behavior on yourself.

According to recent reports, conversations, people and application data all sit in Neon, a serverless Postgres database that scales down to zero and stops costing anything the moment nobody’s using it. The free tier includes enough storage and monthly compute hours for a real early product, with no credit card required to start.

It has been revealed that once the chatbot’s AI agents were actually running, I needed to see what they were doing under the hood: which prompts fired, where they failed, and what they cost. Langfuse traces all of that, and its free Hobby plan includes a healthy monthly allowance of tracing events, enough to debug and monitor a real chatbot without paying anything.

Recent findings suggest that I wired Exa and Firecrawl directly into the AI agents responsible for research inside the chatbot’s runtime, so the chatbot itself can decide when it needs to look something up. Exa handles the search, finding relevant pages for a given question, and its free tier hands new accounts starting credit plus a recurring monthly allowance with no payment method required. It also ships a playground where you can test a search query directly in the browser before wiring it into your agent. Firecrawl handles what comes next, turning a page Exa found into clean text the agent can actually read, and its own free proposal includes a monthly credit allowance with no card needed either.

Sources indicate that before committing to a specific model for the chatbot’s agents, I used NVIDIA’s API Catalog to try several without paying per token. NVIDIA gives any developer free credits to test a wide range of hosted models through its own endpoints, which made it easy to compare options before locking in whichever one actually powers the chatbot in production.

According to recent reports, the chatbot talks back, not just types, so I used Azure AI Speech for text to speech, letting the chatbot switch between a female or male neural voice depending on the setup. The free tier includes a real monthly allowance of neural voice characters at no cost, enough for genuine daily conversations before you’d ever see a bill.

As per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Tech giant, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

Sources indicate that the Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) indicated that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Sources indicate that notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

Recent findings suggest that as per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

Sources indicate that for instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

It has been revealed that later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

During the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

Recent findings suggest that since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Harvard University is not the only top-tier American university that has gained exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market capitalization.

Recent findings suggest that in October 2024, Emory University became the first U.S. university endowment to publicly disclose its holdings in a Bitcoin ETF.

It held roughly 2.7 million shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust, worth over $15 million at the time.

Meanwhile, in May 2025, Brown University disclosed its holdings of 105,000 shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth roughly $4.9 million as of March 31 of that year.

Later, Brown doubled its stake, bringing its holdings to 212,500 shares.

Meanwhile, Dartmouth College has also joined the list of universities with exposure to cryptocurrency ETFs.

In its recent filing, Dartmouth College disclosed that it held 201,531 IBIT shares. The investment was worth roughly $9.5 million as of the end of September 2026.

Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, two prominent AI researchers who spent years at the University of Washington before moving to Stanford, have raised $110 million for Noeri, a startup building AI systems that keep improving on a manufacturer’s own work.

Recent findings suggest that menlo Ventures led the round, with participation from Seattle-based Madrona, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Cisco Investments, Nvidia and Snowflake also invested.

Bloomberg first reported the funding Monday; the valuation wasn’t disclosed.

In a recent development, noeri’s software studies a firm’s data and workflows, then proposes changes to the system around a specific task: the instructions, the tools, which model handles each step and, in some cases, the models themselves. Each change is explained and sent to a person for approval, much like a code review, the company said.

Recent findings suggest that it works with closed and open-weight models. Customers keep ownership of the workflows and models they develop, subject to third-party model licenses, the company said.

According to recent reports, the pitch is aimed at companies stuck choosing between paying for the most capable model and accepting weaker results from a cheaper one. The idea grew partly out of an effort to help a Stanford microbiology and immunology team use OpenAI’s models more cheaply, Bloomberg reported.

The small model they built learned to use older OpenAI models and, to the founders’ surprise, outperformed GPT-5 on that team’s research needs, Choi told Bloomberg.

In a recent development, the name Noeri means “intelligence, in the plural,” reflecting the founders’ argument against a future dominated by one powerful model. Guestrin said at Madrona’s IA40 Summit in late September that intelligence shouldn’t be controlled by one or two companies that own the models.

In a recent development, “Few companies would build their core operations on a single consultant who also advises every competitor, can change its terms at will, and can never be brought in-house,” Choi and Guestrin wrote in an essay posted with the launch. “A single, centralized AI offers exactly that arrangement.”.

Noeri isn’t alone in helping businesses tailor models. In a July report on Noeri’s fundraising, The Information cited Thinking Machines Lab’s Tinker, fine-tuning software that developers use through an API, and Applied Compute, which embeds engineers with its customers.

Guestrin helped develop XGBoost, a widely used machine learning tool, and co-founded Turi, the Seattle startup formerly known as GraphLab and Dato, which Apple acquired in 2016. He went on to lead Apple’s central machine learning and AI organization.

It has been revealed that choi, a 2022 MacArthur Fellow, led common-sense reasoning research at the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) before she left UW and Ai2 in 2024 to join Nvidia as a distinguished scientist, a role she held until starting Noeri in May. She joined Stanford’s faculty in early 2025. The two are co-CEOs.

It has been revealed that noeri is based in Palo Alto with an office in Zurich. Madrona and NEA have backed Guestrin before: the two firms led a $6.75 million round in GraphLab, the startup that became Turi, in 2013.

Anthropic just set an IPO record nobody’s bragging about: $20 billion left on the table

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Anthropic IPO just delivered Wall Street’s AI bulls a strong vote of confidence.
  • Here’s an problem that the bulls are ignoring, and that’s getting virtually no coverage in the media: Anthropic left an enormous share of the IPO’s proceeds on the table.
  • In a recent development, the “left on the table” phenomenon looks amazingly like the scenario surrounding the SpaceX debut in June, though all told, the Anthropic forgone funding number’s even bigger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Anthropic IPO just delivered Wall Street’s AI bulls a strong vote of confidence. The Claude-purveyor’s substantial jump on its opening day of trading for now dispelled fears that investors’ faith in the profitability of this era’s signature technology was fading.

Here’s an problem that the bulls are ignoring, and that’s getting virtually no coverage in the media: Anthropic left an enormous share of the IPO’s proceeds on the table. We’re talking about roughly $20 billion that could have flowed into spending on AI infrastructure that instead went to major institutions, and privileged retail investors, that reaped a gigantic, one-day windfall, as well as the underwriters that will feast on big commissions they’ll receive from the clients they awarded shares at what looks like bargain prices.

In a recent development, the “left on the table” phenomenon looks amazingly like the scenario surrounding the SpaceX debut in June, though all told, the Anthropic forgone funding number’s even bigger. So let’s start by comparing the two offerings. In total amount raised, Anthropic edged SpaceX as the biggest IPO of all time, collecting a headline, gross amount from the shares sold to the public of $81.34 billion versus $75 billion for SpaceX.

Sources indicate that for additional insights into the similarities and contrasts between the two IPOs, I spoke to Jay Ritter, professor at the University of Florida and the world’s leading expert in the field. First, Ritter noted that the percentage fees paid the underwriters are the two lowest numbers he’s ever witnessed, chiefly because the deals are so immense that even at what sounds like a tiny number, the dollars going to the underwriters are the biggest ever collected. The percentages are just a hair apart, 0.666% on SpaceX and 0.676% for Anthropic, a difference of just one-hundredth of 1%. All told, Anthropic is paying the syndicate led by Goldman Sachs $550 million versus $500 million for the SpaceX IPO, where Goldman also served as chief or “lead left” underwriter.

In a recent development, on opening day, SpaceX shares jumped 19.2%. Hence, it collected $14.417 billion less than if it had sold at the price folks and funds were willing to pay—for example, had it deployed a “Dutch auction” instead of a traditional underwriting. That difference, Ritter notes, is known as the “amount left on the table,” or the forgone proceeds. By contrast, the Anthropic pop was slightly lower; shares rose from the offering price of $83 to $97.17 at the close, for a jump of 17.1%. But since Anthropic raised several billions more than SpaceX, the dollars left on the table figure was practically identical at $14.337 billion, or a mere $80 million less.

In a recent development, that near tie doesn’t tell the whole story. In addition to the $81.34 billion offering to the public, Anthropic also conducted a private placement that sold $26 billion in its non-voting N shares to a group including Alphabet, Amazon and Nvidia. When sold, the N shares convert to the regular A voting category. Those legends of tech and other investors also paid 17.1% less than the market judged the shares were worth at day end. That’s an extra $4.4 billion left on the table. Next comes the over-allotment, also known as the “greenshoe.” Selling another 15% of the shares at 17.1% less than the price at the market close amounts to an additional $2 billion “discount” from the price at 4 PM on November 19.

All told, the total comes to just over $20 billion. “Then you include everything, it’s the largest number left on the table in the history of IPOs,” says Ritter. It’s a superlative few on Wall Street are mentioning.

UPDATED 18:41 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Google LLC today released a new version of Gemini’s Mac client that can interact with other apps on the user’s computer.

The feature is available in the U.S. on launch. It requires a Google AI subscription, which equips consumer Google accounts with a broader lineup of artificial intelligence tools. The offering also includes additional storage space and certain other features.

In a recent development, customers can instruct Gemini to launch a local app by including the command “@Computer use” in their prompts. For example, a designer could upload a sketch of a vehicle and ask the AI assistant to turn it into a three-dimensional animation. Gemini finds the local app that is needed for the task, creates a project proposal and carries out the work step by step.

The assistant supports tasks that comprise dozens of actions. Furthermore, consumers can use the output of a newly completed Gemini workflow to launch follow-up projects. A user could have the assistant generate a visual asset in a design tool and then turn it into a mini-app with Visual Studio Code.

Sources indicate that gemini can interact with not only local apps but also web services. That means it can load data from webpages into programs that run on the user’s machine, as well as move data in the opposite direction and between cloud services.

The AI carries out its work in a background window. As a result, customers don’t have to pause their work while the assistant is running. They can track Gemini workflows via a preview pane built into the Mac client’s chat window. Additionally, Google has included controls that make it possible to give Gemini feedback mid-task.

“Privacy and safety are built in: you choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen,” Michael Friedman, Google’s group product manager for the Gemini app, wrote in a blog post.

The Mac version of Muse, Meta Platforms Inc.’s recently rolled out AI agent, can also interact with local apps and data. Furthermore, a cloud-based virtual machine enables it to perform tasks even when the user’s computer is offline. Dots, a competing service from OpenAI Group PBC, offers a similar capability.

According to recent reports, google may seek to match its rivals’ cloud-based workflow hosting features in the future. The organization can also extend Gemini in other ways. Notably, it could bring Gemini’s computer use mode to additional operating systems and add features for business users. OpenAI’s Dots already includes capabilities designed to automate business workflows such as procurement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.
  • In a recent development, in his Nov.
  • The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

In a recent development, in his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz said they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet remarked that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

According to recent reports, some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating newly introduced ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," stated Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a fresh cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz said it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

It has been revealed that "It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz mentioned.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.
  • Recent findings suggest that but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move.
  • It has been revealed that the summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

Recent findings suggest that but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

It has been revealed that the summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

In a recent development, the technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It shows how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

Recent findings suggest that it also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

Sources indicate that A no vote would stop the whole initiative. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 demonstrated an expected result of "Will PASS":.

In a recent development, turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Sources indicate that mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

Recent findings suggest that the tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC demonstrated almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

It has been revealed that the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

Recent findings suggest that the spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence demonstrates what that requirement means on-chain.

So Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the proposal goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 3:00 amNovember 16, 2026 at 12:58 pm.

Fairly, a Portland, Ore.-based vacation rental startup led by Vacasa founder Eric Breon, raised a $22.4 million Series A round, the manufacturer announced Tuesday.

Oregon Venture Fund led the round, with participation from Elevate Capital and Breon.

It has been revealed that fairly pairs vacation rental owners with local caretakers who look after the homes. Its software handles pricing, bookings and scheduling, and uses AI to draft routine guest messages and flag maintenance problems.

Recent findings suggest that guests booked more than $66 million in reservations through Fairly over the past year, up from about $5 million the year before, the firm said. Nearly 900 caretakers now manage about 2,000 homes across 47 states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

It has been revealed that owners pay a single 20% fee, which Fairly splits with the caretaker, compared with the 25% to 40% the organization says other managers typically charge. Fairly also says it doesn’t tack extra fees onto guest bills, so guests pay less overall.

It has been revealed that “At Vacasa, I led a 7,000-person team, and delivering quality, individualized care at that scale is not an easy task,” Breon said in a statement. “At Fairly, we take a completely different approach: we empower dedicated, hyperlocal caretakers to care for homes, and our systems do the heavy lifting around them.”.

Breon founded Vacasa in Portland in 2009 and spent more than a decade there. The company went public via a SPAC deal in 2021 and was acquired in May 2025 by Phoenix-based Casago, a vacation rental manager.

Recent findings suggest that fairly, founded in 2023, emerged from stealth in December 2024 with $10.1 million in pre-seed funding. The company has now raised $32.5 million in total.

Fairly now employs 106 people, up from 25 at its launch in 2024. Co-founder Subechya Person remains chief product officer; co-founder and former CTO Jeff Flitton left the tech giant in February.

XRP price could bottom out at $0.78, according to analyst Ali Martinez.

Industry observers note that in a recent post on X, Martinez shared a chart with what appears to be an ascending triangle pattern. The triangle's closest low is at $0.78.

Sources indicate that XRP has already fallen 43% from its October high of $1.55. According to Martinez, the correction might continue until the price reaches the bottom.

If the price holds $0.78, a possible bull run toward $3.50 might follow.

"A weekly breakout above $3.50, followed by a successful retest as support, could confirm the multi-year ascending triangle and trigger a bull run to $18," Martinez wrote.

The RSI fell below 25 before the latest recovery, which suggests oversold conditions.

A rebound following a massive sell-off does not equal a trend reversal.

In October, the 200 EMA acted as strong resistance that XRP was unable to break.The $1 mark is the first psychological threshold XRP needs to reclaim, acting as both support and resistance.

Major Institutional Milestone for XRP: XRPL Becomes First Public Blockchain to Pass Global Financial Infrastructure Standards Assessment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zycrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The XRP Ledger (XRPL) has scored a major institutional milestone that could bolster its appeal to traditional financial institutions as demand for blockchain-based financial infrastructure grows.
  • The XRP Ledger Foundation has announced that the network is the first public, permissionless Layer-1 blockchain to have its Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.
  • The XRP Ledger’s latest achievement could mark an crucial step toward strengthening its position in the institutional blockchain market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) has scored a major institutional milestone that could bolster its appeal to traditional financial institutions as demand for blockchain-based financial infrastructure grows.

The XRP Ledger Foundation has announced that the network is the first public, permissionless Layer-1 blockchain to have its Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The XRP Ledger’s latest achievement could mark an crucial step toward strengthening its position in the institutional blockchain market. On November 13, the independent attestation report detailing XRPL’s assessment under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit was released, highlighting the network’s willingness to measure its infrastructure against standards designed for traditional financial markets and emerging digital asset systems.

The toolkit provides a common framework for evaluating blockchain networks across 10 key principles, including governance, legal foundations, settlement finality, architecture, operational resilience, cybersecurity, interoperability, and privacy. These criteria are particularly relevant to banks, asset managers, and other regulated institutions exploring blockchain technology to support tokenized deposits, stablecoins, investment funds, and other financial instruments.

Notably, the XRP Ledger Foundation conducted a self-assessment covering all 10 principles, while blockchain security firm CertiK independently reviewed the supporting evidence for the Architecture and Resiliency principles. Its verification involved reviewing technical evidence—including code, system configurations, logs, and test results—to determine whether selected controls were implemented as described.

It has been revealed that the development could give financial institutions a more structured reference point when evaluating XRPL for institutional-grade financial applications. However, the assessment does not amount to full GL1 certification or regulatory approval, meaning prospective institutional users will still need to conduct their own due diligence.

The Global Layer One initiative brings together leading financial institutions and policymakers to establish common standards for digital financial infrastructure. It aims to streamline cross-border transactions involving tokenized assets while ensuring that blockchain networks meet internationally recognized requirements for financial market infrastructure.

The latest development may strengthen the XRP Ledger’s prospects among traditional financial institutions considering blockchain-based financial solutions. Potential use cases include tokenized deposits, stablecoins, investment funds, and capital-market instruments. The GL1 assessment framework incorporates globally recognized financial market guidelines, drawing on CPMI-IOSCO principles and established digital asset control standards.

The review also provides institutions with a clearer framework for examining XRPL’s technical infrastructure, operational resilience, and suitability for financial applications. To maintain its relevance, the XRP Ledger Foundation intends to revisit the assessment periodically, taking into account future network improvements and changes in global industry requirements.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The holiday shopping season is in full swing — and it started early this year.
  • Latest data from specialized point-of-sale software tech giant Quilt Software, which serves more than 20,000 independent retailers, from jewelers and pet stores to liquor stores and grocers, highlighted a 7.6% same-store sales growth spike in October year over year.
